title: Friedelin suppresses osteoclastogenesis via sequential dual-targeting of p105 processing and STAT3-mediated metabolic reprogramming.
authors: Zhang, Xuanrui; Yang, Biao; Ma, Xiaoyu; Zhang, Weijin; Xu, Xunpei; Zhan, Haoqin; Zhang, Zhanrong; Zhou, Xuhui; Zhang, Zheng; Tao, Zhengbo
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Friedelin抑制破骨细胞生成的双靶点机制，核心是蛋白-蛋白互作与代谢重编程，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，且方法以实验为主，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pathological osteolysis, driven by excessive osteoclast activity, is a hallmark of Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) and osteoporosis. Current therapies target inflammation but fail to prevent bone erosion, highlighting the demand for dual-action agents. Although Tripterygium wilfordii has shown therapeutic efficacy in RA, its clinical application is restricted by toxicity. Consequently, identifying novel bioactive monomers with favorable safety and deciphering their targets remains a critical need. METHODS: Through network pharmacology, we identified Friedelin as a core bioactive monomer of Tripterygium wilfordii. Its anti-osteoclastogenic efficacy was evaluated in vitro and validated in vivo using collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) and ovariectomized (OVX) mouse models. To elucidate direct targets and molecular mechanisms, we integrated RNA-seq, cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA), surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and molecular docking. RESULTS: Friedelin potently suppresses RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation throughout the full course of induction in vitro. Mechanistically, Friedelin directly targets both p105(NF-kappaB1) and STAT3 exerting sequential pharmacological effects. During the early phase of differentiation, its binding to p105 inhibits ubiquitination-dependent processing, thereby aborting NF-kappaB signaling initiation. Subsequently, in the late phase, its interaction with STAT3 disrupts the STAT3/NFATc1 transcriptional and STAT3/LDHB metabolic axes, leading to impaired osteoclastogenesis. In vivo, Friedelin exhibited superior efficacy to Methotrexate (MTX) in alleviating bone erosion in CIA mice and effectively prevented bone loss in OVX mice. CONCLUSION: Friedelin acts as a potent dual-phase inhibitor of osteoclastogenesis by sequentially blocking p105 dependent signaling initiation and STAT3 mediated transcriptional regulation. This study highlights Friedelin as a promising therapeutic candidate for inflammatory and metabolic bone diseases.
abstract_zh: 背景：由过度破骨细胞活性驱动的病理性骨溶解是类风湿关节炎（RRA）和骨质疏松症的一个标志性特征。当前疗法针对炎症但未能阻止骨侵蚀，凸显了对双重作用药物的需求。尽管雷公藤（Tripterygium wilfordii）在RA中显示出治疗功效，但其临床应用受毒性限制。因此，识别具有良好安全性的新型生物活性单体并阐明其靶点仍是关键需求。方法：通过网络药理学，我们鉴定出弗里德林（Friedelin）为雷公藤的核心生物活性单体。其抗破骨细胞生成功效在体外进行了评估，并在体内使用胶原诱导性关节炎（CIA）和去卵巢（OVX）小鼠模型进行了验证。为阐明直接靶点和分子机制，我们整合了RNA-seq、细胞热位移分析（CETSA）、表面等离子体共振（SPR）和分子对接。结果：弗里德林在体外诱导全程中有效抑制RANKL诱导的破骨细胞分化。机制上，弗里德林直接靶向p105(NF-kappaB1)和STAT3，发挥序贯药理学效应。在分化早期阶段，其与p105的结合抑制泛素化依赖性加工，从而阻断NF-kappaB信号启动。随后，在晚期阶段，其与STAT3的相互作用破坏STAT3/NFATc1转录轴和STAT3/LDHB代谢轴，导致破骨细胞生成受损。在体内，弗里德林在缓解CIA小鼠骨侵蚀方面表现出优于甲氨蝶呤（MTX）的功效，并有效预防OVX小鼠的骨丢失。结论：弗里德林通过序贯阻断p105依赖性信号启动和STAT3介导的转录调控，作为破骨细胞生成的有效双阶段抑制剂。本研究强调弗里德林是炎症性和代谢性骨疾病的有前景治疗候选药物。
